name: Graph Explorer
type: MOL
section: graphs
why: A worker draws the far field into one canvas and decides which few hundred nodes get DOM, so a million-node graph stays a bounded page; every node, label and panel you read is plain, themed, keyboard-reachable HTML.
when: Exploring large connected data - service maps, data lineage, knowledge graphs, dependency graphs - by semantic zoom, search and drill-down. For a schematic you draw by hand, diagram; for a small text-defined diagram, mermaid; for a tree of records, data-tree.
where: dist/components/graphs.css + dist/components/graphs.js (the extra bundle - load it after all.css / all.js; per component: dist/components/graph-explorer/graph-explorer.css + graph-explorer.js)
supportedStates: default, selected, focused

# Pattern: Graph Explorer

## Native basis

A `<div class="graph-explorer">` becomes one focusable `role="application"`
viewport. A Web Worker started from the component's own source owns the graph:
the hierarchy of clusters, the layouts, the cycles and every dot and bulk edge,
drawn into an `OffscreenCanvas` and handed over as an `ImageBitmap`. The main
thread keeps a bounded pool of DOM slots - chips and cards for the nodes worth
reading, labels along the edges - and morphs them only when their markup
changes. The rest of an explorer's interface (breadcrumb, search, outline,
details, relations, a Node UI switch) are **outlets**: elements the page places
where it likes - typically Panels of a Border Layout - that the runtime fills.

## Native Web APIs

- [Web Workers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API) + [`Blob` URLs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/createObjectURL_static) - the graph lives off the main thread; a classic Blob worker also starts inside an opaque-origin sandbox
- [`OffscreenCanvas`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/OffscreenCanvas) + [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ImageBitmapRenderingContext) - the worker draws the far field; the bitmap moves to the page without a copy
- [Transferable objects](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API/Transferable_objects) - bitmaps and tier arrays cross threads for free
- [`requestAnimationFrame()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/requestAnimationFrame) - one clock for the bitmap and the DOM writes
- [Pointer Events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Pointer_events) + [`setPointerCapture()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/setPointerCapture) - pan, pinch, press and hold
- [`wheel`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/wheel_event) - zoom anchored at the cursor
- [Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API) - the keyboard map
- [`ResizeObserver`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ResizeObserver) + [`MutationObserver`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MutationObserver) - the viewport refits; attributes written from outside apply at once
- [`translate`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/translate) + [`contain`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/contain) - slots move on the compositor, the viewport's layout stays its own
- [CSS masks](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/mask) - the icons: one empty element each, painted in the current color
- [Relative colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_colors/Relative_colors) + [`color-mix()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/color-mix) - type colors and tints from the theme's chart tokens
- [`@starting-style`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@starting-style) - nodes fade in as they get DOM
- [WAI-ARIA combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) - the search outlet; the outline is a [tree](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/)
- [`prefers-reduced-motion`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion) / [`prefers-contrast`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-contrast) / [`forced-colors`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors) - jumps instead of flights, stronger strokes, system colors (also on the canvas)

---

## Structure

```html
<div class="graph-explorer" id="kg" data-nodes="100000" data-seed="7" data-frame aria-label="Service graph"></div>
```

- `data-nodes` - the size of the synthetic graph, 2,000 to 4,000,000 (default
  `1000000`); `data-seed` - its seed (default `7`): the same seed builds the same
  graph, so ids are stable across loads.
- Ids name nodes: `c<number>` a cluster (`c0` is the top), `n<number>` an entity.
- `data-selected="c4 c9"` - the selected nodes; `data-selected-edge="c4>c9"` -
  the selected link (`<source id>><target id>`, two nodes of the view; nodes and
  a link are never selected together); `data-focus="c12"` - the cluster the view
  is in; `data-node-ui="health"` - the Node UI; `data-expanded` - the
  selection's full page in the details outlet. These are the state.
- `data-hud` - a performance overlay (nodes, DOM, canvas, worker timing).
- `data-frame` - a border and radius when it stands alone (in a Panel the panel
  is the frame).
- Its height: `100%` of its container, at least `--graph-explorer-min-height`
  (default `20rem`); a Panel body that holds it gives it all its room.

### Outlets and outputs

Anything the page binds with `data-graph-explorer-for="<id>"` - the element
itself or one inside it:

| Attribute | The runtime puts in it |
| --- | --- |
| `data-graph-explorer-outlet="breadcrumb"` | a Breadcrumb of the path to the view; a crumb moves up |
| `data-graph-explorer-outlet="search"` | a search combobox over every node (the scan runs in the worker); a result flies there |
| `data-graph-explorer-outlet="outline"` | a filterable tree of the view's children (the biggest first) |
| `data-graph-explorer-outlet="details"` | the detail renderer's view of the first selected node or of the selected link; expanded, its full page |
| `data-graph-explorer-outlet="relations"` | a Table of its relations, each link drawn by the edge label renderers (a click on one inspects it); for a link, its single links |
| `data-graph-explorer-outlet="node-ui"` | a switch of the Node UIs (Labels, Health, Compact, the plugins') |
| `data-graph-explorer-output="details-title"` | the details title (the authored text while nothing is selected) |
| `data-graph-explorer-output="relations-title"` | the selected node's name and its relation count ("Identity · 5"), for a link the names of both ends and its count (the authored text while nothing is selected); the label beside it is the page's |
| `data-graph-explorer-output="view"` | the view's name |
| `data-graph-explorer-output="status"` | the announcements (the explorer's own live region when there is none) |
| `data-graph-explorer-action="up"` / `fit` / `live` / `help` / `collapse` | move up, fit, start / stop the live breaker simulation (`aria-pressed`), the keyboard map, back from an expanded page |

Inside the explorer, renderers write `data-graph-explorer-action="enter"` /
`bring` / `expand` / `collapse` / `details` (acting on their node or the
selected link), `data-graph-explorer-goto="<id>"` (fly there - on an expanded
page: that node's page, so a page drills down into the next) and
`data-graph-explorer-edge="<source id>><target id>"` (select that link).

A click on a link - its label or its line - selects it: the rest of the graph
steps back and the details show its traffic both ways, the relations it carries,
the circuit breakers it bundles, who sends and who receives most; `E` or a
double click expands it, `Esc` lets it go.

Expand maximizes the **Panel** that holds the details outlet (and restores it
on the way back); a Panel holding the relations outlet renders it when it
unfolds. The whole application - toolbar north, outline west, the graph in the
center, details east, relations south - is a Border Layout of Panels on the
page:

```html
<div class="border-layout" data-frame="none" style="block-size: 40rem">
  <header class="border-layout-north flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2">
    <div class="flex-1 min-w-0" data-graph-explorer-for="kg" data-graph-explorer-outlet="breadcrumb"></div>
    <div class="w-full max-w-80" data-graph-explorer-for="kg" data-graph-explorer-outlet="search"></div>
    <button class="btn" data-variant="outline" data-size="sm" type="button" data-graph-explorer-for="kg" data-graph-explorer-action="fit">Fit</button>
  </header>
  <div class="resizer border-layout-west" data-min="160" data-max="420">
    <section class="card panel" style="width: 15rem" aria-labelledby="kg-outline-t">
      <header class="panel-header"><h3 class="panel-title" id="kg-outline-t">Outline</h3></header>
      <div class="panel-body" data-flush data-graph-explorer-for="kg" data-graph-explorer-outlet="outline"></div>
    </section>
  </div>
  <section class="card panel border-layout-center" aria-labelledby="kg-graph-t">
    <header class="panel-header"><h3 class="panel-title" id="kg-graph-t">Graph</h3>
      <div class="panel-tools" data-graph-explorer-for="kg" data-graph-explorer-outlet="node-ui"></div></header>
    <div class="panel-body" data-flush><div class="graph-explorer" id="kg" data-nodes="1000000" aria-label="Service graph"></div></div>
  </section>
  <div class="resizer border-layout-east" data-min="240" data-max="640">
    <section class="card panel" style="width: 23rem" aria-labelledby="kg-details-t">
      <header class="panel-header"><h3 class="panel-title" id="kg-details-t" data-graph-explorer-for="kg" data-graph-explorer-output="details-title">Details</h3>
        <div class="panel-tools"><label class="swap panel-maximize">...</label></div></header>
      <div class="panel-body" data-graph-explorer-for="kg" data-graph-explorer-outlet="details"></div>
    </section>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Plugins

`df$.shadcn.graphExplorer.register(scope, plugin)` - `scope` is `'global'` or one
explorer (its plugins win). A renderer is a pure function of its input that
returns `ctx.html` markup (every interpolation escaped; `on*` attributes, URLs
that run code and active elements are stripped):

- **node** - `match(node)` returns a score or `false`, `sizes: { chip, card }`,
  `render(node, ctx)` per tier (`ctx.tier` is `chip` or `card`). With `variant`
  it belongs to a Node UI the switch offers; without one it serves every Node UI.
- **edge** - `rules`: plain data the worker evaluates for every link it draws
  (`{ when: [{ field: 'breaker.state', equals: 'open' }], style: { tone: 'danger', width: 2, gap: true } }`);
  `label`: DOM labels along links in three tiers (`icon`, `label`, `full`)
  picked by the link's length on screen, budgeted, never overlapping;
  `detail`: `{ match(item), title(item), render(item, ctx) }` - the details of a
  selected link (`item.source`, `item.target`, `item.edge`; its numbers from
  `ctx.fetchEdge(item.id)`).
- **detail** - `render(node, ctx)` for the details outlet; `ctx.expanded` asks
  for the node's full page. Anything async goes through `ctx.request(key, load)`,
  which renders the node again when the value arrives. `page(node)` returning
  false says a node has no page; `ctx.expandable` is true only where a page can
  show (a details outlet, and a renderer that offers one) - an Expand button
  belongs only there (an edge `detail` takes `page(item)` the same way).

The details are markup the runtime morphs on every change. A library component
with a script inside them - a Chart, a Geo Map, an Avatar - goes in
`ctx.island(key, markup)`: an island keeps its element, and what its script
made, while its key and its markup stay the same. `ctx.island(key, markup, mount)`
also runs `mount(el)` once when the island's element is made - bind a Data Grid's
records or a chart's data there - and the function it returns when the island
goes. `ctx.fetchRows(id)` answers every row behind a node or a link, built by
the worker: the entities below a cluster (id, label, type, system, domain,
owner, out, in, rows, freshness) or a link's single links both ways (from, to,
relation, direction, the systems).

```html
<!-- a detail renderer's markup: CSS-only components inline, a Chart in an island -->
<dl class="graph-explorer-stats"><div class="graph-explorer-stat"><dt>p95</dt><dd>63 ms</dd></div></dl>
<div class="graph-explorer-island" data-graph-explorer-island="latency:c26">
  <div class="chart" data-size="sm" role="img" aria-label="p95 latency" data-chart='{"xAxis":{"type":"category","data":["0h","1h","2h"]},"yAxis":{"type":"value"},"series":[{"type":"line","data":[61,63,58]}]}'></div>
</div>
```

The built-in plugins draw clusters and entities in three Node UIs (`default` =
Labels, `health`, `compact`), relation labels, circuit breakers (one per link
between entities, health by share on links between clusters) and the details of
a node and of a link - side and expanded - from the library's Badge, Button,
Card, Statistic, Table and Data Grid and the explorer's own parts. An expanded
cluster page holds every entity below it in a Data Grid, an expanded link page
every single link both ways; beside the grid, dataview aggregations of the
grid's own source show how the rows its filters match split up (by type, owner,
the largest systems; by relation, way, the busiest senders) and follow every
filter; a name in the grid opens its page. Without `df$.shadcn.dataGrid` loaded
the pages keep sample tables. The explorer's parts (`graph-explorer-stats`,
`-section`, `-rows` / `-row`, `-bar`, `-shares`, `-trail`, `-page`,
`-kpis`, `-page-grid`, `-records`), which plugins use the same way.
The icons are `ctx.icon(name)` - a Lucide subset as CSS masks;
`registerIcon(name, shapes)` adds one.

## Variants

| Attribute | Values | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-node-ui` | `default` (Labels), `health`, `compact`, a plugin's | how nodes are drawn; `V` cycles, the node-ui outlet switches |
| `data-frame` | *(present)* | a border and a radius around the viewport |
| `data-hud` | *(present)* | the performance overlay |

## Sizes

| Attribute | Values | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-size` on `.graph-explorer-icon` | `xs` (0.75rem), `sm` (0.875rem), `lg` (1.5rem), `xl` (2rem) | an icon's size; without it 1rem (`ctx.icon(name, { size })`) |

## ARIA

| Attribute | Where | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `role="application"` + `aria-roledescription="graph"` | the `.graph-explorer` (generated) | one tab stop that takes the keys: arrows move the focus to the nearest node in that direction, Enter enters, Space selects, `?` opens the map |
| `aria-describedby` | the `.graph-explorer` (generated) | the keyboard map |
| `aria-label` | the `.graph-explorer` | names the graph |
| `aria-label` | a details row's link button (generated) | "Inspect the link to *name*": the keyboard way to a link |
| `aria-busy="true"` | the `.graph-explorer`, while the worker builds the graph | not final yet |
| `role="combobox"` + `aria-activedescendant` | the search outlet's input (generated) | the APG combobox: arrows walk the results, Enter flies to one |
| `role="tree"` / `treeitem` | the outline outlet (generated) | the path and the view's children; arrows walk, Enter acts |
| live region | the status output, else the explorer's own `<output>` | the view, the keyboard focus, Bring & Go |

## Notes

- The page never holds more than a bounded set of nodes: at most 120 cards, 300
  chips and 200 edge labels, however large the graph.
- The data is a synthetic service graph the worker builds from the seed -
  domains, systems (API, Worker, Store, Stream) and entities (Dataset, Endpoint,
  Document, Person, Job, Topic), linked by calls, reads and owns, with cycles and
  circuit breakers. The renderers, the outlets and the State API do not depend on
  it.
- Zooming into a cluster until it fills most of the viewport enters it; zooming
  out, or panning off its disk, moves up. Search, the breadcrumb, the outline and
  the relations fly there with a smooth zoom-pan (a jump under reduced motion).
- The names the worker draws beside small nodes are measured, and the edge
  labels keep clear of them.
- Expand shows only where a page can show: an explorer without a details outlet
  draws its cards without the Expand button, and E or `expanded: true` only
  select (the state lands unexpanded).
- The canvas, the slots, the labels and every outlet's content are the runtime's
  (`data-ce-chrome`): render() and the HTML Preview Editor see only the
  element's attributes and the outlets as authored.
- Theme changes re-read the colors for the canvas; forced colors draw it in
  system colors.

## States

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | The top level, nothing selected |
| `selected` | `config.selected` nodes - or the link `config.edge` - picked at the top level (an id deeper down flies there - the state lands in `focused`) |
| `focused` | Inside the cluster `config.focus`, with or without a selection there |

```js
const graph = document.querySelector('#kg');
await graph.api.settled();                                   // the worker built the graph
await graph.api.setState('focused', { focus: 'c3' });        // enter cluster c3
await graph.api.setState('focused', { focus: 'c3', selected: ['c41'], expanded: true }); // its child's full page
await graph.api.setState('selected', { edge: 'c3>c7' });     // the link between two domains
graph.api.setState('default', { nodeUi: 'health' });         // back to the top, health bars
graph.api.getState(); // { name: 'default', config: { focus: null, selected: [], nodeUi: 'health', expanded: false, edge: null } }
```

The registry global is `df$.shadcn.graphExplorerApi` /
`df$.shadcn.graphExplorerStates`; the explorer API is `df$.shadcn.graphExplorer`.

### Every element

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| <code>el.api.setState&lt;S extends GraphExplorerState&gt;(name: S, config?: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[S]): unknown</code> | Enter a state: the DOM work runs (also when it is the current state), the store records it. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>name</code></td><td><code>S</code></td><td>a declared state (an unknown name throws)</td></tr><tr><td><code>config?</code></td><td><code>GraphExplorerStateConfigs[S]</code></td><td>that state's config (merged into the stored one when the component merges)</td></tr></table> <b>Returns</b> <code>unknown</code> - what the state's DOM work returned - a Promise for an async state (or await settled()) |
| <code>el.api.getState(): { name: GraphExplorerState; config: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[GraphExplorerState]; model?: ElementModel }</code> | The state the element shows now - read back from the DOM, so it includes what the user changed. <b>Returns</b> <code>{ name: GraphExplorerState; config: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[GraphExplorerState]; model?: ElementModel }</code> - the state's name, its config and the authored markup model render() starts from |
| <code>el.api.render(state?: { name: GraphExplorerState; config: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[GraphExplorerState]; model?: ElementModel }): string</code> | The element's markup in a state - the authored markup with that state applied; a pure function of the state. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>state?</code></td><td><code>{ name: GraphExplorerState; config: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[GraphExplorerState]; model?: ElementModel }</code></td><td>a state as getState() returns it (default: the current one)</td></tr></table> <b>Returns</b> <code>string</code> - the element's outer HTML in that state |
| <code>el.api.settled(): Promise&lt;void&gt;</code> | Wait for the last state's DOM work (async states: a diagram rendering, a chart mounting). <b>Returns</b> <code>Promise&lt;void&gt;</code> - resolves when nothing is pending |
| <code>el.store: Store&lt;{ name: GraphExplorerState; config: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[GraphExplorerState] }&gt;</code> | A defuss-store store of the element's state - subscribe to follow every change (also the user's), set it to drive the component. |

| <code>df$.shadcn.graphExplorerApi.store(el: HTMLElement): Store&lt;{ name: GraphExplorerState; config: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[GraphExplorerState] }&gt;</code> | The element's store (bindComponent made it). <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>el</code></td><td><code>HTMLElement</code></td><td>the component's element</td></tr></table> <b>Returns</b> <code>Store&lt;{ name: GraphExplorerState; config: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[GraphExplorerState] }&gt;</code> - a defuss-store store of { name, config } - subscribe to follow every change, set it to drive the component |
| <code>df$.shadcn.graphExplorerApi.commit&lt;S extends GraphExplorerState&gt;(el: HTMLElement, name: S, config?: GraphExplorerStateConfigs[S]): void</code> | Record a state the element reached on its own (no DOM work) - for a component's own handlers. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>el</code></td><td><code>HTMLElement</code></td><td>the component's element</td></tr><tr><td><code>name</code></td><td><code>S</code></td><td>the state it is in</td></tr><tr><td><code>config?</code></td><td><code>GraphExplorerStateConfigs[S]</code></td><td>its config</td></tr></table> |
| <code>df$.shadcn.graphExplorerStates: GraphExplorerState[]</code> | The declared states, 'default' first: <code>default</code>, <code>selected</code>, <code>focused</code>. |

| Member | Description |
|---|---|

Explorers on the page render again with it. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>scope</code></td><td><code>'global' \| HTMLElement \| string</code></td><td>'global', or the .graph-explorer element (or its selector)</td></tr><tr><td><code>plugin</code></td><td><code>GraphPlugin</code></td><td>the plugin</td></tr></table> <b>Returns</b> <code>()</code> - a function that removes the plugin again |

| <code>fit(target: string \| HTMLElement): Promise&lt;string&gt;</code> | Fits the view's whole cluster into the viewport. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>target</code></td><td><code>string \| HTMLElement</code></td><td>the .graph-explorer element or its selector</td></tr></table> <b>Returns</b> <code>Promise&lt;string&gt;</code> - 'done', or 'interrupted' when another flight took over |
| <code>flyTo(target: string \| HTMLElement, camera: GraphCamera): Promise&lt;string&gt;</code> | Flies the camera to a point of the view's unit disk. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>target</code></td><td><code>string \| HTMLElement</code></td><td>the .graph-explorer element or its selector</td></tr><tr><td><code>camera</code></td><td><code>GraphCamera</code></td><td>the camera to land on</td></tr></table> <b>Returns</b> <code>Promise&lt;string&gt;</code> - 'done', or 'interrupted' when another flight took over |

| <code>selectEdge(target: string \| HTMLElement, id: string \| null): void</code> | Selects a link of the view (null clears it): its details show and the rest of the graph steps back. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>target</code></td><td><code>string \| HTMLElement</code></td><td>the .graph-explorer element or its selector</td></tr><tr><td><code>id</code></td><td><code>string \| null</code></td><td>the link: '&lt;source id&gt;&gt;&lt;target id&gt;' of two nodes in the view, or null</td></tr></table> |
| <code>setNodeUi(target: string \| HTMLElement, name: string): void</code> | Shows another Node UI: 'default' (Labels), 'health', 'compact' or a plugin's. <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>target</code></td><td><code>string \| HTMLElement</code></td><td>the .graph-explorer element or its selector</td></tr><tr><td><code>name</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>the Node UI's name</td></tr></table> |

| <code>expand(target: string \| HTMLElement, id: string): Promise&lt;void&gt;</code> | Expands a node's full page: its detail renderer with ctx.expanded, the details outlet's Panel maximized (navigates there first when the node is not in view). <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>target</code></td><td><code>string \| HTMLElement</code></td><td>the .graph-explorer element or its selector</td></tr><tr><td><code>id</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>the node's id, or a link's ('&lt;source id&gt;&gt;&lt;target id&gt;')</td></tr></table> <b>Returns</b> <code>Promise&lt;void&gt;</code> - resolves when the page shows |

| <code>simulate(target: string \| HTMLElement, on: boolean): void</code> | Starts or stops the live circuit-breaker simulation (breakers trip, probe and close on their own). <table><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>target</code></td><td><code>string \| HTMLElement</code></td><td>the .graph-explorer element or its selector</td></tr><tr><td><code>on</code></td><td><code>boolean</code></td><td>true to start, false to stop</td></tr></table> |

### Events

| Event | Description |
|---|---|
| `graph-explorer-action` | an action button was used <code>detail</code>: <code>GraphExplorerActionDetail</code> <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>action</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>the action: enter, bring, expand, collapse, details, up, fit, live, help</td></tr><tr><td><code>id</code></td><td><code>string \| null</code></td><td>the node it acted on, null for the explorer's own actions</td></tr></table> |
| `graph-explorer-error` | the worker or a renderer failed <code>detail</code>: <code>GraphExplorerErrorDetail</code> <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>message</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>what failed</td></tr></table> |
| `graph-explorer-focus` | the view moved to another cluster (null = the top) <code>detail</code>: <code>GraphExplorerFocusDetail</code> <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>focus</code></td><td><code>string \| null</code></td><td>the cluster's id, null at the top</td></tr><tr><td><code>path</code></td><td><code>GraphPathStep[]</code></td><td>the path from the top to it</td></tr></table> |
| `graph-explorer-node-ui` | another Node UI is shown <code>detail</code>: <code>GraphExplorerNodeUiDetail</code> <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>nodeUi</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>its name</td></tr></table> |
| `graph-explorer-select` | the selection changed - by a click, a key, a search result or setState <code>detail</code>: <code>GraphExplorerSelectDetail</code> <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>selected</code></td><td><code>string[]</code></td><td>the selected node ids</td></tr><tr><td><code>edge</code></td><td><code>string \| null</code></td><td>the selected link ('&lt;source id&gt;&gt;&lt;target id&gt;'), null when nodes or nothing is selected</td></tr></table> |
| `graph-explorer-view` | the camera came to rest <code>detail</code>: <code>GraphExplorerViewDetail</code> <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>focus</code></td><td><code>string \| null</code></td><td>the cluster the view is in, null at the top</td></tr><tr><td><code>camera</code></td><td><code>GraphCamera</code></td><td>the camera</td></tr></table> |

### Types

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `GraphBreaker` | The breaker facts of a link: one circuit breaker, or the worst of the many an aggregated link bundles. <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>state</code></td><td><code>'closed' \| 'half-open' \| 'open' \| 'cut'</code></td><td>closed (healthy), half-open (probing), open (tripped) or cut (by hand)</td></tr><tr><td><code>trips</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>trips counted</td></tr><tr><td><code>since</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>minutes since the breaker left closed</td></tr><tr><td><code>probes</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>probes a half-open breaker sends</td></tr><tr><td><code>probesOk</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>probes that succeeded</td></tr><tr><td><code>by</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>who cut it</td></tr><tr><td><code>open</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>member breakers open</td></tr><tr><td><code>half</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>member breakers half-open</td></tr><tr><td><code>cut</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>member breakers cut</td></tr><tr><td><code>members</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>breakers the link bundles</td></tr><tr><td><code>aggregate</code></td><td><code>boolean</code></td><td>true when the link bundles several breakers (an edge between clusters)</td></tr><tr><td><code>openShare</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the share of open members, 0 to 1</td></tr><tr><td><code>badShare</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the share of members not closed, 0 to 1</td></tr></table> |
| `GraphBreakerCounts` | A cluster's breakers by state, summed over its links at this level. <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>open</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>open breakers</td></tr><tr><td><code>half</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>half-open breakers</td></tr><tr><td><code>cut</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>cut breakers</td></tr><tr><td><code>total</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>breakers in all</td></tr></table> |
| `GraphCamera` | The camera: where the view's unit disk is shown. <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>cx</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the center, in the view's unit disk</td></tr><tr><td><code>cy</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the center, in the view's unit disk</td></tr><tr><td><code>z</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>screen px per unit</td></tr></table> |
| `GraphCondition` | One condition of an edge rule; every condition of a rule must hold. <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>field</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>the edge field, dotted for nested ones: 'kind', 'type', 'breaker.state', 'breaker.openShare'</td></tr><tr><td><code>equals?</code></td><td><code>string \| number \| boolean</code></td><td>the value must equal this</td></tr><tr><td><code>in?</code></td><td><code>(string \| number \| boolean)[]</code></td><td>the value must be one of these</td></tr><tr><td><code>exists?</code></td><td><code>boolean</code></td><td>the value must exist (true) or be missing (false)</td></tr><tr><td><code>gte?</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the value must be at least this</td></tr><tr><td><code>lte?</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the value must be at most this</td></tr></table> |
| `GraphDetails` | What the worker knows about a node beyond its view: path, relations, counts. <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>id</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>the node's id</td></tr><tr><td><code>path</code></td><td><code>GraphPathStep[]</code></td><td>the path from the top to the node</td></tr><tr><td><code>relations?</code></td><td><code>GraphRelation[]</code></td><td>a cluster's relations at its level, the busiest first (at most 60)</td></tr><tr><td><code>members?</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>a cluster's entities</td></tr><tr><td><code>children?</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>a cluster's direct children</td></tr><tr><td><code>level?</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>a cluster's hierarchy level</td></tr><tr><td><code>out?</code></td><td><code>GraphLink[]</code></td><td>an entity's outgoing links (at most 40)</td></tr><tr><td><code>in?</code></td><td><code>GraphLink[]</code></td><td>an entity's incoming links (the sources; at most 40)</td></tr><tr><td><code>outDeg?</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>an entity's outgoing links in all</td></tr><tr><td><code>inDeg?</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>an entity's incoming links in all</td></tr></table> |
| `GraphEdge` | A link between two nodes of the view. <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>k</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>its index in the view</td></tr><tr><td><code>a</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the index of its source node in the view</td></tr><tr><td><code>b</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the index of its target node in the view</td></tr><tr><td><code>count</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>links from a to b (an aggregate counts its members)</td></tr><tr><td><code>count2</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>links from b to a</td></tr><tr><td><code>bidir</code></td><td><code>boolean</code></td><td>true when it runs both ways</td></tr><tr><td><code>back</code></td><td><code>boolean</code></td><td>true when it is the back-edge of a cycle</td></tr><tr><td><code>kind</code></td><td><code>'leaf' \| 'agg'</code></td><td>'leaf' between entities, 'agg' between clusters (it bundles the links below)</td></tr><tr><td><code>type</code></td><td><code>string</code></td><td>the relation: calls, reads or owns</td></tr><tr><td><code>breaker</code></td><td><code>GraphBreaker \| null</code></td><td>its breaker facts (null when it has none)</td></tr><tr><td><code>traffic</code></td><td><code>boolean</code></td><td>true while traffic flows (the live simulation)</td></tr><tr><td><code>style</code></td><td><code>GraphEdgeStyle</code></td><td>how the rules draw it</td></tr></table> |
| `GraphEdgeContext` | What an edge label renderer gets besides the edge. <table><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td><code>tier</code></td><td><code>'icon' \| 'label' \| 'full'</code></td><td>icon, label or full - picked by the edge's length on screen, the budgets and the free space</td></tr><tr><td><code>depth</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the hierarchy level of the view (0 = the top)</td></tr><tr><td><code>zoom</code></td><td><code>number</code></td><td>the camera's zoom</td></tr><tr><td><code>view</code></td><td><code>string \| null</code></td><td>the view's id</td></tr><tr><td><code>html</code></td><td><code>(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]) =&gt; SafeHtml</code></td><td>the escaping template tag</td></tr><tr><td><code>icon</code></td><td><code>(name: string, options?: GraphIconOptions) =&gt; SafeHtml</code></td><td>an icon</td></tr><tr><td><code>source?</code></td><td><code>GraphNode</code></td><td>the link's source node (labels in the graph)</td></tr><tr><td><code>target?</code></td><td><code>GraphNode</code></td><td>the link's target node (labels in the graph)</td></tr><tr><td><code>selected?</code></td><td><code>boolean</code></td><td>true when an end of the link is selected</td></tr></table> |
